sentiment.rationale: The document reports strong Q3 results (net income up 12% YoY, EPS up 16% YoY) and management describes the quarter as 'strong' with each line of business performing well. However, forward guidance for NII ex. Markets in 2026 is a preliminary central case of ~$95B, which is below the consensus of ~$100B that management notes 'does look a little bit low.' The full-year 2025 NII ex. Markets guidance was raised to ~$92.2B from the prior ~$91B (implied by the Q4 outlook of ~$23.5B added to the 9-month actual of $68.7B), but the 2026 preliminary view is a headwind. Management also flags significant uncertainty around geopolitical conditions, tariffs, and sticky inflation. The net effect is a mildly positive score, as the backward-looking beat and modest guidance raise for 2025 are partially offset by the cautious 2026 outlook and risk commentary.

summary.revenue: Reported revenue of $46.4 billion; managed revenue of $47.1 billion, up 9% YoY.
summary.eps: Earnings per share (diluted) of $5.07, up 16% YoY.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 NII ex. Markets implied at ~$92.2B (Q4 outlook ~$23.5B + 9-month actual $68.7B). Preliminary 2026 NII ex. Markets central case of ~$95B. Full-year 2025 adjusted expense implied at ~$95.9B (Q4 outlook ~$24.5B). 2025 Card NCO rate expected to be ~3.3%.
summary.margin: Reported overhead ratio of 52%; managed overhead ratio of 52%. ROTCE of 20%.
key_risks: Heightened uncertainty from complex geopolitical conditions, tariffs and trade uncertainty, elevated asset prices and the risk of sticky inflation.
Wholesale charge-offs slightly elevated due to apparent fraud in certain secured lending facilities (e.g., Tricolor $170mm charge-off).
Deposit margin compression and impact of lower rates on NII.
Higher compensation and expense growth driven by revenue-related compensation, growth in front office employees, and inflation (including medical costs up 10% next year).
key_opportunities: Investment Banking fees up 16% YoY with robust pipeline and upbeat client sentiment.
Markets revenue up 25% YoY, with record third-quarter Markets revenue of nearly $9 billion.
Strong net inflows in AWM ($109 billion AUM net inflows) and record first-time investors in wealth management.
Continued strong net new checking account acquisitions (over 400,000 this quarter).
Potential for regulatory relief from Basel III Endgame revisions and other capital rule changes.
